thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — hitting a weird duping of request IDs in the Node SDK when the built-in retry triggers. Steps to repro below.
leo: ugh, that sounds messy. does it happen only with the retry middleware or on any retry path?
maria: confirmed with our http-retry layer and also with axios-retry in sampleapp. When retry happens, logs show the same req-id on both attempts, then our trace shows parent/child confusion.
jordana: can you paste the log snippet? also which SDK version?
maria: SDK @ 1.7.2, sampleapp pinned to node 18. snippet:

```
2026-03-20T18:42:10Z maria INFO request_id=abc123 start request POST /v1/generate
2026-03-20T18:42:11Z maria WARN request_id=abc123 retry attempt 1
2026-03-20T18:42:11Z maria INFO request_id=abc123 start request POST /v1/generate
```

maria: expected new request_id on the retried attempt, or at least a retry_id appended. instead we keep overwriting the same id which confuses redaction and tracing.
sara: hmm might be an OpenTelemetry context propagation issue — if we re-use the same span context across retries the loghook will keep the same trace/request id.
alex: is the Node SDK using async_hooks or manual context passing? that changes race cases.
maria: Node SDK uses async_hooks + otel shim in the autoinit hook. My suspicion is hook ordering: the retry wrapper runs before our otel hook attaches a fresh context for the new attempt.
leo: that matches a race we've seen with other middleware. We changed hook order in the Python shim by ensuring retry wrapper clones context. Node might not have parity.
jordana: can you try forcing a new reqid in the retry middleware as a short-term workaround? e.g., on retry create new headers: { 'x-request-id': generate() }
maria: did that locally — it fixes log ambiguity but the trace still ties back to original span, so the tracing UI shows two requests under one trace which is borderline ok but not ideal for SLI counting.
sara: also redaction: currently we redact using the request_id token, and because it's duplicated we sometimes redact the wrong lines when two attempts overlap in logs. can we make redaction operate on log entry-level unique ids instead of propagated req-id?
alex: implementation-wise that means adding a log-local uuid per emission (a log_event_id) in the SDK's log hook. lowers risk of cross-request bleed. but it's a breaking schema change for downstream parsers.
leo: maybe we can add it as opt-in header/log field first: LOG_EVENT_ID or x-log-event-id. non-breaking and gives us data to evaluate.
maria: agreed. plan suggestion: 1) short-term: retry middleware injects new x-request-id on each attempt; 2) mid-term: add optional LOG_EVENT_ID to log hook and expose via SDK opts; 3) long-term: rework otel hook ordering so that the tracing context for a retry attempt is isolated (parity with Python behavior).
jordana: i'll own the mid-term change (log_event_id opt-in) and add feature flag in SDK config.
sara: i'll take a look at the otel hook ordering and see if we can detect retries and create child spans instead of reusing same span id.
alex: i'll update sampleapp to demonstrate retry-id injection and add a small CI test that asserts distinct x-request-id headers for retry attempts (very small e2e).
ops-bot: ticket created: DE-1248 "Node SDK: distinct request IDs and log_event_id opt-in for retries" (assigned: jordana)
maria: thanks all. note: also saw this crop up with our hosted proxy for a specific auth retry code when KMS was slow — so it's not just axios. worth a broader fix.
leo: quick question — should we also redact x-request-id when it's present in logs? current redaction patterns only look for `request_id=` formatted tokens, not headers.
jordana: i'll update redaction rules to scan for common header forms (x-request-id, X-Request-Id, request-id) and the new LOG_EVENT_ID.
sara: fyi, I'll coordinate with infra to ensure otel collector doesn't collapse spans for retried requests (we saw a collector rule that merges by trace id decades ago).
alex: i'll open a PR for sampleapp and CI test this afternoon, tagging @jordana and @sara for review.
maria: if anyone wants to repro quickly, here's a tiny curl script that flips a 503 on first attempt in sampleapp so you can see the duplicate id behavior: 

```
# curl + temporary server that returns 503 then 200
curl -H "x-request-id: manual-try-1" http://localhost:3000/generate
```

maria: thanks, will follow up once PRs land. :thumbsup:
devex-bot: Reminder: please add CHANGELOG entry under "devex" for any opt-in logging changes.
maria: noted, will do.
ops-bot: deployment queued for sampleapp-retry-fix (staging) — ETA 12m
maria: closing loop — staging looks good, distinct x-request-ids on retries, trace child spans created by otel hook change. will schedule a short postmortem writeup for DE-1248.
